cases.purpose: S1. A pending approval whose capability is revoked before the approval attempt: the approve, the issue and the start are denied, nothing is approved or issued, and the tool is never invoked.
S2. Non-vacuity control for S1: the same pending lineage without any revocation is approved, issued and started (approval_granted, permit_issued and execution_started at their own steps).
The terminal commit fence on its own: a commit through the retained context after the terminal is denied, without any revocation that could mask it. The first commit shows commits work (non-vacuity).

Control run: the tool returns a pending native Promise whose settlement the runtime cannot observe. The correct outcome is missing terminal evidence; a reported terminal (for example premature) is a failure.

incomplete: terminal evidence missing for e1 in window 1..2

declared_incomplete: terminal evidence missing for e1 in window 1..2

cases.purpose: S5. An ancestor revoked before its descendant is ever used: the descendant's start is denied and the tool is never invoked (no approve or issue operation). Package-1 witness of M20.
S6. Non-vacuity control for S5: the same issuer-signed chain without any revocation starts the descendant, so S5's denial is caused by the ancestor revocation, not by a chain rejection.
S7. A pending approval whose tenant is revoked before the approval attempt: the approve, the issue and the start are denied, and the tool is never invoked.
S8. A pending approval of a descendant whose ancestor is revoked before the approval attempt: the approve, the issue and the start are denied, and the tool is never invoked.

S9. Tenant revocation of in-flight work: the commits before the cut stay, the covered execution is signalled (cancellation acknowledged) and its delivery is withheld; the other tenant's execution in a session of the same name delivers. Witness of M28 (delivery) and M29 (cancellation signal).

S10. Ancestor revocation of in-flight work: the commits before the cut stay, the covered descendant is signalled and its delivery is withheld; an unrelated authority in the same session delivers. Witness of M35 (delivery) and M36 (cancellation signal).

S11. A session revocation covers a pending approval: the approve, the issue and the start of a (revoked session) are denied; b, pending in another session of the same tenant, is approved, issued and started (non-coverage).

S12. A tenant revocation covers an issued, unused permit: both permits are issued before the revocation; the start of a (revoked tenant) is denied, the start of b (another tenant, a session of the same name) runs.
S13. An ancestor revocation covers a descendant's issued, unused permit: the start of c (child of the revoked p) is denied, the start of q (no parent) runs.
S14. An ancestor revocation between a descendant's approval and its issue: the approval granted before the revocation stays; the issue and the start are denied.
